# komorebi-render API

komorebi-render queues videos of sunlight through leaves and runs komorebi's pinned WebGL2 exporter on the Mac mini's GPU.
There is one worker, so jobs queue. The API and worker run together with `komorebi-render serve`.
The default address is http://<mini's tailnet name or IP>:8077; KOMOREBI_RENDER_HOST defaults to 0.0.0.0.
There is no authentication yet. Use the LAN or tailnet; authentication must precede Cloudflare exposure.
Responses are JSON except GET /llms.txt. Examples below use `base=http://jojo-m4-mini:8077`.

## Job spec

POST the spec itself, without a wrapper. Exactly one of `preset` or `look` is required; `size` and `seconds` are required.
Unknown top-level fields are refused. Defaults apply to omitted optional fields.

| Field | Limits and default |
| --- | --- |
| `preset` | String `<positive id>[@positive version][:share]`, such as `3`, `3@2` or `3:share`. Without a version, the exporter pins the head on first run. A share token opens an unlisted preset and is redacted in responses. Private presets need the worker's ARBORETUM_TOKEN or KOMOREBI_RENDER_ARBORETUM_TOKEN_FILE. |
| `look` | Object with `look.params` and optional `look.name`; exactly one of preset or look. |
| `look.params` | An object of editor params, as saved by komorebi. Required for a look job. |
| `look.name` | Optional string; unnamed looks are called `look`. |
| `size` | `1080p`, `4k`, or even `WxH` from 64x64 through 7680x4320. Aliases normalize to 1920x1080 and 3840x2160. No default. |
| `seconds` | Whole number, 1 to KOMOREBI_RENDER_MAX_SECONDS (default maximum 21600 = 6 hours). No default. |
| `fps` | 30 or 60; default 60. |
| `master` | Boolean, default false. True keeps lossless segments; false deletes them only after delivery verification. |
| `quality` | `authored` (default), `max`, or an object of the four fields below. An empty object is authored. |
| `quality.tex_resolution` | 1024, 2048, 4096. Omitted: the look's saved value. |
| `quality.bake_resolution` | 0, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048. 0 follows tex_resolution. Omitted: the look's saved value. |
| `quality.sample_count` | Whole number from 16 to 48. Omitted: the look's saved value. |
| `quality.ss` | 1, 2. Default 1 for authored/custom. Renders at this multiple and downscales. |
| `delivery` | Optional object: choose vt_bitrate or vt_quality, not both. Omitted or empty uses the exporter's 60M bitrate default, with a 75M cap and 120M buffer. |
| `delivery.vt_bitrate` | Positive bitrate string with k, K or M, such as `60M`, `80M` or `8000k`. Lowercase m is refused because ffmpeg reads it as milli. |
| `delivery.vt_quality` | Whole number 0 to 100; mutually exclusive with vt_bitrate. |

Only quality keys become --set or --ss; the look stays as authored. Max means tex_resolution 4096, bake_resolution 0,
sample_count 48 and ss 2 at 1080p or smaller (ss 1 above 1080p). Max costs about 300 ms/frame on the M4; authored costs
about 15 ms/frame at 1080p or 37 ms/frame at 4K. Max at 1080p is about 20 times authored. One hour of max at 60 fps can
take about 18 hours to render; such jobs are normal and are not refused because of cost.

Preset example:
```json spec
{"preset":"3@2","size":"1080p","seconds":30}
```
Look example:
```json spec
{"look":{"name":"Autumn Gold","params":{}},"size":"4k","seconds":60,"fps":30}
```
Quality and delivery example:
```json spec
{"preset":"3","size":"1080p","seconds":300,"quality":{"tex_resolution":2048,"bake_resolution":1536,"sample_count":32,"ss":2},"delivery":{"vt_bitrate":"80M"}}
```

## Routes

POST /jobs — validate and queue; 201 with id, state and folder. The folder is null if no output root is configured.
```sh
curl -sS "$base/jobs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"preset":"3@2","size":"1080p","seconds":30,"quality":"max"}'
```
```json
{"id":1,"state":"queued","folder":"/Volumes/home/komorebi/jobs/2026-10-10-1-preset-3"}
```

GET /jobs — newest first, wrapped in `jobs`; each summary has id, state, name (preset or look), size, seconds, fps,
resolved quality, progress, eta_s, eta_basis, blocked and timestamps.
```sh
curl -sS "$base/jobs"
```
```json
{"jobs":[{"id":1,"state":"queued","name":"preset 3@2","size":"1920x1080","seconds":30,"fps":60,"quality":{"name":"max","set":{"tex_resolution":4096,"bake_resolution":0,"sample_count":48},"ss":2},"progress":{"done":0,"total":3,"fraction":0},"eta_s":540,"eta_basis":"estimate","blocked":null,"created_at":"2026-10-10T10:00:00Z","started_at":null,"finished_at":null}]}
```

GET /jobs/:id — summary fields above plus redacted spec, folder, delivery (path, size_mib, mbit_s), error,
last_line, log_tail (last 20 lines), quality_vs_master from the manifest when measured, cancel_requested and attempts.
Fields without a result are null; log_tail is empty before a run. The example shows the additional fields; summaries remain.
```sh
curl -sS "$base/jobs/1"
```
```json
{"id":1,"state":"done","folder":"/Volumes/home/komorebi/jobs/2026-10-10-1-preset-3","delivery":{"path":"/Volumes/home/komorebi/jobs/2026-10-10-1-preset-3/delivery.mp4","size_mib":212.8,"mbit_s":59.5},"spec":{"preset":"3@2","size":"1920x1080","seconds":30,"fps":60,"master":false,"quality":"max"},"error":null,"last_line":"done","log_tail":["delivery verified","done"],"quality_vs_master":null,"cancel_requested":false,"attempts":1}
```

DELETE /jobs/:id — queued jobs cancel immediately (200); running jobs request cancellation (202), then the worker stops
the exporter. The folder is kept. A completed, failed or already cancelled job returns 409; an unknown id returns 404.
```sh
curl -sS -X DELETE "$base/jobs/1"
```
```json
{"id":1,"cancel":"requested","state":"running"}
```
For a queued job: `{"id":1,"cancel":"cancelled","state":"cancelled"}`.

GET /health — 200 with ok, the pinned commit, worker (idle, busy or blocked), and nas (ok or missing).
`ok` means the API is responding; inspect nas and worker before assuming a job can run.
```sh
curl -sS "$base/health"
```
```json
{"ok":true,"pin":"6d3ee0ad83c0f5254f2ef2045037b732c3197fbf","worker":"idle","nas":"ok"}
```

GET /llms.txt — 200, text/plain; this document.
```sh
curl -sS "$base/llms.txt"
```
The response starts with `# komorebi-render API`.

## Polling, refusals and outputs

Poll GET /jobs/:id no faster than every 10 seconds. States are `queued`, `running`, `done`, `failed` and `cancelled`.
`progress.done` counts completed 10-second segments; `progress.total` is ceil(seconds / 10). `eta_s` is seconds remaining
for this job, not queue waiting time. `eta_basis` is `estimate` until a segment from the current attempt finishes, then
`measured` from that attempt's segment rate. Terminal states have null ETA. A restart resumes unfinished segments.

A missing, unwritable or non-network NAS keeps the job `queued` with `blocked` explaining why; the worker retries when
the share returns. It does not render onto the Mac's disk and does not fail the job just because the share is missing.
An engine that cannot prepare also leaves a queued job blocked. A render failure sets `failed` and retains its folder and log.
Read the run.log tail before resubmitting a failed job, and never resubmit blindly. Long jobs take hours: trust the ETA.

A refused spec is 422 with `error` and `field` (null for the whole spec), plus `errors` listing all field/error pairs:
```sh
curl -sS "$base/jobs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"preset":"3","size":"1080p","seconds":0}'
```
```json
{"error":"seconds must be a whole number from 1 to at most 21600","field":"seconds","errors":[{"field":"seconds","error":"seconds must be a whole number from 1 to at most 21600"}]}
```
Invalid JSON is 400; a body over 1048576 bytes is 413. Unknown routes/jobs are 404, wrong methods 405, unexpected errors 500.
Preset share tokens and the worker's arboretum token never appear in responses or logs.

Outputs land in KOMOREBI_RENDER_OUT, normally /Volumes/home/komorebi/jobs, under `<yyyy-mm-dd>-<id>-<slug>/`.
Preset slugs use only the id; look slugs use the name. Each job leaves delivery.mp4, manifest.json and run.log.
seg/ holds lossless masters only when master is true; look-input.json is the preserved input for a look job.
The delivery path is a filesystem path on the NAS, not an HTTP download URL.
